name: Baccaurea macrocarpa
tagline: A rare tropical rainforest fruit tree valued for its nutritious and medicinal fruit.
description: Baccaurea macrocarpa, commonly known as Tampoi, is a tropical fruit tree native to Southeast Asia. It is widely found in regions of Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand. The tree produces edible antioxidant-rich fruits that are appreciated for their sweet and slightly tangy taste. Traditionally, different parts of the plant have been used in folk medicine for digestive support and for minor skin-related conditions.
origin: Tropical Southeast Asia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand
medical: Antioxidant-rich, digestive aid, anti-inflammatory properties. Folk medicine reports topical use for minor swelling or skin issues.

name: Morus nigra
tagline: A nutrient-rich mulberry tree valued for its sweet fruits and traditional medicinal benefits.
description: Morus nigra, commonly known as Brazilian Mulberry or Black Mulberry, is a fruit-bearing tree originally native to Western Asia, especially Persia. The tree produces dark, sweet berries that are rich in Vitamin C, minerals, dietary fiber, and water content, making them nutritious and refreshing. Traditionally, different parts of the plant, especially the leaves, have been valued for their antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and digestive-supporting properties.
medical: Rich in Vitamin C, minerals, dietary fiber, and water content with low calories and moderate sugar. Contains phytochemicals with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Leaf compounds may help inhibit digestive enzymes.
